pluss::subsp::stats::ts::kpss_test¶

The KPSS test of the null that a series is stationary around a level or a trend.

Signature¶

ts::KpssResult ts::kpss_test(const pluss::Series& y, const ts::KpssOptions& options = {}, pluss::codem::Config cfg = {});

What It Does¶

kpss_test removes a constant (trend = false) or a constant and a linear trend (trend = true, the default) from the series, accumulates the residuals, and compares the size of the accumulated sum with the long-run variance of the residuals. Rejecting the null means the series is not stationary around that deterministic part: it has a unit root, or a trend that was not modelled. The p-value is interpolated from the test’s critical-value table and is bounded by its extremes (0.01 and 0.10).

The long-run variance estimate needs a bandwidth. lags = 0 uses the plain residual variance, which is right only if the series has no autocorrelation; a series with positive autocorrelation then looks non-stationary. Set lags to a bandwidth that reflects the series’s memory (a few lags for a persistent series; a common rule is about 4 (n / 100)^{1/4}). Read together with adf_test: they have opposite nulls.

Parameters¶

const pluss::Series& y

The series to test, in time order.

const ts::KpssOptions& options

lags (bandwidth of the long-run variance, default 0), trend (test stationarity around a trend, default true) and alpha (default 0.05); see KpssOptions.

pluss::codem::Config cfg

Output configuration (dtype and platform of the returned series); the computation itself runs in double precision.

Returns¶

A KpssResult: the statistic, the p-value, the critical value at alpha, reject, the long-run variance used, the lags used and the observations used.

Errors¶

  • lags must be smaller than the series length.

Practical Examples¶

Example 1¶

A random walk is rejected as stationary; an autoregression is judged with a bandwidth that reflects its memory.

#include <pluss/ma.h>

#include <cmath>
#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

namespace ts = pluss::subsp::stats::ts;
using pluss::Series;

const auto f64 = pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
void show(const char* label, const Series& s) {
  std::cout << std::left << std::setw(14) << label << std::right << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4);
  for (double v : s.host<double>()) std::cout << std::setw(9) << v;
  std::cout << "\n";
}
std::vector<double> noise(int n) {
  std::vector<double> e(n);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    double u = std::sin(12.9898 * (i + 1.0) + 78.233) * 43758.5453;
    u -= std::floor(u);
    e[i] = u - 0.5;
  }
  return e;
}
Series ar1(int n, double phi) {
  const auto e = noise(n);
  std::vector<double> x(n);
  double carry = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    carry = phi * carry + e[i];
    x[i] = carry;
  }
  return pluss::make_series(x, {n}, f64);
}
Series walk(int n) {
  const auto e = noise(n);
  std::vector<double> x(n);
  double sum = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    sum += e[i];
    x[i] = sum;
  }
  return pluss::make_series(x, {n}, f64);
}

int main() {
  const Series stationary = ar1(200, 0.7);
  const Series unit_root = walk(200);
  ts::KpssOptions options;
  options.lags = 8;
  for (const auto* s : {&stationary, &unit_root}) {
    const auto r = ts::kpss_test(*s, options);
    std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4) << (s == &stationary ? "AR(1)       " : "random walk  ") << "statistic " << r.stat << "  p = " << r.pvalue << "  critical " << r.critical
              << "  stationarity rejected: " << std::boolalpha << r.reject << "\n";
  }
}

Output

AR(1)       statistic 0.1056  p = 0.1000  critical 0.1460  stationarity rejected: false
random walk  statistic 0.3562  p = 0.0100  critical 0.1460  stationarity rejected: true

Example 2¶

The bandwidth matters for a persistent series: with no lags the long-run variance is too small and the statistic too large.

#include <pluss/ma.h>

#include <cmath>
#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

namespace ts = pluss::subsp::stats::ts;
using pluss::Series;

const auto f64 = pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
void show(const char* label, const Series& s) {
  std::cout << std::left << std::setw(14) << label << std::right << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4);
  for (double v : s.host<double>()) std::cout << std::setw(9) << v;
  std::cout << "\n";
}
std::vector<double> noise(int n) {
  std::vector<double> e(n);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    double u = std::sin(12.9898 * (i + 1.0) + 78.233) * 43758.5453;
    u -= std::floor(u);
    e[i] = u - 0.5;
  }
  return e;
}
Series ar1(int n, double phi) {
  const auto e = noise(n);
  std::vector<double> x(n);
  double carry = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    carry = phi * carry + e[i];
    x[i] = carry;
  }
  return pluss::make_series(x, {n}, f64);
}
Series walk(int n) {
  const auto e = noise(n);
  std::vector<double> x(n);
  double sum = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    sum += e[i];
    x[i] = sum;
  }
  return pluss::make_series(x, {n}, f64);
}

int main() {
  const Series y = ar1(200, 0.7);
  for (int lags : {0, 4, 8}) {
    ts::KpssOptions options;
    options.lags = lags;
    const auto r = ts::kpss_test(y, options);
    std::cout << "lags " << lags << "  long-run variance " << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4) << r.long_run_var << "  statistic " << r.stat << "\n";
  }
}

Output

lags 0  long-run variance 0.1391  statistic 0.4478
lags 4  long-run variance 0.4185  statistic 0.1489
lags 8  long-run variance 0.5900  statistic 0.1056

Example 3¶

trend = false tests stationarity around a constant level instead of a trend.

#include <pluss/ma.h>

#include <cmath>
#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

namespace ts = pluss::subsp::stats::ts;
using pluss::Series;

const auto f64 = pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
void show(const char* label, const Series& s) {
  std::cout << std::left << std::setw(14) << label << std::right << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4);
  for (double v : s.host<double>()) std::cout << std::setw(9) << v;
  std::cout << "\n";
}
std::vector<double> noise(int n) {
  std::vector<double> e(n);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    double u = std::sin(12.9898 * (i + 1.0) + 78.233) * 43758.5453;
    u -= std::floor(u);
    e[i] = u - 0.5;
  }
  return e;
}
Series ar1(int n, double phi) {
  const auto e = noise(n);
  std::vector<double> x(n);
  double carry = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    carry = phi * carry + e[i];
    x[i] = carry;
  }
  return pluss::make_series(x, {n}, f64);
}
Series walk(int n) {
  const auto e = noise(n);
  std::vector<double> x(n);
  double sum = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    sum += e[i];
    x[i] = sum;
  }
  return pluss::make_series(x, {n}, f64);
}

int main() {
  const Series y = ar1(200, 0.7);
  ts::KpssOptions level, trend;
  level.lags = trend.lags = 8;
  level.trend = false;
  std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4) << "level: statistic " << ts::kpss_test(y, level).stat << ", critical " << ts::kpss_test(y, level).critical << "\n";
  std::cout << "trend: statistic " << ts::kpss_test(y, trend).stat << ", critical " << ts::kpss_test(y, trend).critical << "\n";
}

Output

level: statistic 0.1703, critical 0.4630
trend: statistic 0.1056, critical 0.1460
